title: 2021年6月四级真题 第2套 阅读1
paperTitle: 2021年6月大学英语四级真题（第2套）
passage:
P1 Sugar shocked. That describes the reaction of many Americans this week following revelations that, 50 years ago, the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists for research that shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat.

P2 What might surprise consumers is just how many present-day nutrition studies are still funded by the food industry. Nutrition scholar Marion Nestle of New York University spent a year informally tracking industry-funded studies on food. "Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest," Nestle tells us. Other systematic reviews support her conclusions.

P3 For instance, studies funded by Welch Foods—the brand behind Welch's 100% Grape Juice— found that drinking Concord grape juice daily may boost brain function. Another, funded by Quaker Oats, concluded, as a Daily Mail story put it, that "hot oatmeal(燕麦粥) breakfast keeps you full for longer."

P4 Last year, The New York Times revealed how Coca-Cola was funding well-known scientists and organizations promoting a message that, in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink. Coca-Cola also released data detailing its funding of several medical institutions and associations between 2010 and 2015.

P5 "It's certainly a problem that so much research in nutrition and health is funded by industry," says Bonnie Liebman, director of nutrition at the Center for Science in the Public Interest. "When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for." And what it pays for is often a pro- industry finding.

P6 Given this environment, consumers should be skeptical(怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science and ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed. "Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence," Liebman says, pointing to the official government Dietary Guidelines, which are based on reviews of hundreds of studies.

P7 "And that expert advice remains pretty simple," says Nestle. "We know what healthy diets are— lots of vegetables, not too much junk food, balanced calories. Everything else is really difficult to do experimentally."

questions.q: What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago?
options: They raised public awareness of the possible causes of heart disease.
They turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat.
They placed the sugar industry in the spotlight with their new findings.
They conducted large-scale research on the role of sugar in people's health.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago? 问的是过去某个具体行为，答案应是定位 段对该行为的客观陈述。

【拆句】What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago? 是 what 引导的一般疑问句，主语 Harvard scientists，时间状语 50 years ago，结构平铺直叙，无陷阱。

【定位】Sugar shocked. That describes the reaction of many Americans this week following revelations that, 50 years ago, the sugar industry paid Harvard scientists for research that shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat. 糖业震惊。这描述了本周许多美国人在得知一桩内幕后的反应——50 年前，糖业出钱请哈 佛科学家做研究，把心脏病的责任焦点从糖身上挪开，狠狠地压在了膳食脂肪头上。 46. What did Harvard scientists do 50 years ago? A) They raised public awareness of the possible causes of heart disease. B) They turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat. C) They placed the sugar industry in the spotlight with their new findings. D) They conducted large-scale research on the role of sugar in people's health.

【选项】A) 无中生有 raised public awareness of the possible causes of heart disease 说哈佛科学家"提高 了公众对心脏病病因的认知"，但原文只说他们"转移焦点"，从未提及"提高认知"，且行 为方向相反——是误导而非启蒙。 B) ✓ 正确 shifted the focus away from sugar's role in heart disease—and put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat ↔turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat 预判内容"把心脏病矛头从糖转向脂肪"与 turned public attention away from the health risks of sugar to fat 在框架、对象、方向上完全重合，即同义替换型正确项。 C) 与原文相反 placed the sugar industry in the spotlight with their new findings 说研究让"糖 业"成为焦点，与原文 put the spotlight(注意的中心) squarely on dietary fat 恰恰相 反——焦点是脂肪而非糖业。 D) 无中生有 conducted large-scale research on the role of sugar in people's health 强调"大规 模"研究，但原文未提及研究规模，只说糖业出钱资助；且研究内容不是"糖与健康的作 用"而是"转移焦点"。 Marion Nestle对当今营养学研究有何看法? A) 这些研究花了她整整一年时间来追踪和分析。 B) 它们大多基于系统性综述。 C) 它们依赖于食品行业的资助。 D) 几乎所有研究都服务于资助方的目的。

questions.q: What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies?
options: They took her a full year to track and analyze.
Most of them are based on systematic reviews.
They depend on funding from the food industries.
Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies? 直接索取一个人对 一事的具体说法，答案应是文中该人原话的转述。

【拆句】What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies? 主干 What...does Marion Nestle say，about 引出宾语补足语限定 say 的内容范围；句法直白。

【定位】"Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest," Nestle tells us. Nestle 告诉我们："在近 170 项研究里，约 90% 的结果都偏向了资助方的利益。" 47. What does Marion Nestle say about present-day nutrition studies? A) They took her a full year to track and analyze. B) Most of them are based on systematic reviews. C) They depend on funding from the food industries. D) Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders.

【选项】A) 答非所问 They took her a full year to track and analyze 说"研究花了她一整年追踪"，对应原文 spent a year informally tracking，但这是关于 Nestle 的研究方法，不是她 对"present-day nutrition studies"本身的看法，答非所问。 B) 张冠李戴 Most of them are based on systematic reviews 把"systematic reviews"安 到"present-day nutrition studies"头上，但原文 Other systematic reviews support her conclusions 是说"其他系统性综述支持 Nestle 的结论"，systematic reviews 是支 持她的工具，不是被她评论的研究的本质。 C) 偷换概念 They depend on funding from the food industries 说"研究依赖食品业资助"，是"资 金来源"层面的事实，而原文 Nestle 强调的是"研究结论偏向资助方"——把"结论偏 袒"偷换成了"资金依赖"。两者层面不同。 D) ✓ 正确 Roughly 90% of nearly 170 studies favored the sponsor's interest ↔ Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders 预判"九成研究服务资助方利益"与 Nearly all of them serve the purpose of the funders 在数量级、动作、对象三层全部对齐，是教科书级同义替换正确项。 可口可乐资助的研究声称什么? A) 运动对健康的重要性超过饮食。 B) 选择吃什么和喝什么是控制体重的关键。 C) 饮用可口可乐不会导致体重增加。 D) 食品行业在对抗肥胖方面发挥着重要作用。

options: Exercise is more important to good health than diet.
Choosing what to eat and drink is key to weight control.
Drinking Coca-Cola does not contribute to weight gain.
The food industry plays a major role in fighting obesity.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim? 问被可口可乐资助的研究主张了什么，答案 是文中明示的论断。

【拆句】What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim? 主语 Coca-Cola-funded studies 是"名词- funded 复合形容词+名词"结构，意为"被可口可乐资助的研究"；句意直白。

【定位】Last year, The New York Times revealed how Coca-Cola was funding well-known scientists and organizations promoting a message that, in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink. 去年《纽约时报》披露，可口可乐资助知名科学家和组织，宣扬这样一种主张：在对抗体重 增长的战斗中，人们应更看重运动，而不是吃了什么、喝了什么。 48. What did Coca-Cola-funded studies claim? A) Exercise is more important to good health than diet. B) Choosing what to eat and drink is key to weight control. C) Drinking Coca-Cola does not contribute to weight gain. D) The food industry plays a major role in fighting obesity.

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 in the battle against weight gain, people should pay more attention to exercise and less to what they eat and drink ↔Exercise is more important to good health than diet 预判"重运动而轻饮食"与 Exercise is more important to good health than diet 的"运 动比饮食更重要"严格等价；定位句的 more/less 平行结构本身就是隐性比较。 B) 与原文相反 Choosing what to eat and drink is key to weight control 说"吃喝选择是控重关键"， 与原文 less to what they eat and drink"少在乎吃喝"完全相反——可口可乐研究恰恰 要弱化饮食责任。 C) 无中生有 Drinking Coca-Cola does not contribute to weight gain 凭空捏造一句"喝可乐不会 增重"，原文从未出现此论断；可口可乐资助研究只是"转移注意力"到运动，并未直接为 可乐本身辩护。 D) 偷换概念 The food industry plays a major role in fighting obesity 说"食品业在抗肥胖中起重 要作用"，看似与原文相关，但原文是说"可口可乐资助研究让人忽视饮食"，并未把食品 业塑造为"抗肥胖功臣"；把"产业操纵议程"偷换成了"产业贡献抗肥胖"。 Liebman对行业资助的研究有何看法? A) 它只关注营养和健康。 B) 它在消费者中造成困惑。 C) 它很少产生客观的研究结果。 D) 它违背公共利益。

questions.q: What does Liebman say about industry-funded research?
options: It simply focuses on nutrition and health.
It causes confusion among consumers.
It rarely results in objective findings.
It runs counter to the public interest.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does Liebman say about industry-funded research? 同 Q47 同款句式，仍是细节 题，定位到 Liebman 引语即可。

【拆句】What does Liebman say about industry-funded research? 结构同 Q47；industry- funded 是"名词-过去分词"复合形容词，表被动"被产业资助的"。

【定位】"When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for." And what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding. "当食品业出钱做研究时，它常常能买到自己想要的结论。"而它想买的，往往是一个对产业 有利的结果。 49. What does Liebman say about industry-funded research? A) It simply focuses on nutrition and health. B) It causes confusion among consumers. C) It rarely results in objective findings. D) It runs counter to the public interest.

【选项】A) 答非所问 It simply focuses on nutrition and health 只说研究"聚焦营养健康"，是话题描述，未 触及 Liebman 对"业内资助偏袒"的核心评价；属答非所问。 B) 无中生有 It causes confusion among consumers 说"造成消费者困惑"，原文 P5 Liebman 谈的 是"研究结论偏袒产业"，未提及消费者困惑这一后果——"困惑"是后文（P6）作者建议 引出的语境，但不是 Liebman 的直接评价。 C) ✓ 正确 what it pays for is often a pro-industry finding ↔It rarely results in objective findings When the food industry pays for research, it often gets what it pays for ↔ It rarely results in objective findings 预判"买到的多是偏袒产业的结论"与 It rarely results in objective findings 是同一事实 的正反描述：常偏袒=极少客观。 D) 过度推断 It runs counter to the public interest 跨越"研究偏袒产业"直接推到"与公众利益对 立"——这是合理但过度的引申。原文只说结论亲产业，没有明示"对立于公众利益"， 且 Liebman 所在机构名 Center for Science in the Public Interest 是机构名而非她的 论断。 作者对消费者的建议是什么? A) 在决定吃什么时遵循自己的直觉。 B) 对饮食专家的建议持怀疑态度。 C) 忽略新闻推送中的无关信息。 D) 对新的营养学研究发现要三思而后行。

questions.q: What is the author's advice to consumers?
options: Follow their intuition in deciding what to eat.
Be doubtful of diet experts' recommendations.
Ignore irrelevant information on their news feed.
Think twice about new nutrition research findings.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the author's advice to consumers? 问的是一项具体行动建议，答案是文末作者 明示的劝告，仍属细节题（非笼统主旨）。

【拆句】What is the author's advice to consumers? What is 主系表结构，主语 the author's advice，介词短语 to consumers 修饰 advice 表对象；无难点。

【定位】Given this environment, consumers should be skeptical(怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science and ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed. 鉴于这种环境，消费者读到营养科学的最新发现时应当保持怀疑，并对新闻推送里冒出来的 最新研究置之不理。 50. What is the author's advice to consumers? A) Follow their intuition in deciding what to eat. B) Be doubtful of diet experts' recommendations. C) Ignore irrelevant information on their news feed. D) Think twice about new nutrition research findings.

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Follow their intuition in deciding what to eat 让消费者"凭直觉决定吃什么"，与原文 末段 Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence（依赖审过全部证据 的健康专家）方向相反——作者要的是依赖权威而非凭直觉。 B) 与原文相反 Be doubtful of diet experts' recommendations 让消费者"怀疑膳食专家的建议"，但 原文恰恰相反 Rely on health experts who've reviewed all the evidence——要怀疑 的是"业内出资的最新研究"，不是"健康专家"。 C) 偷换概念 Ignore irrelevant information on their news feed 让消费者"忽略新闻推送里的无关信 息"，但原文 ignore the latest study that pops up on your news feed 让消费者忽略 的是"新闻推送里冒出的最新研究"——把"最新研究"偷换成"无关信息"，对象被偷偷扩大 并改性质。 D) ✓ 正确 consumers should be skeptical(怀疑的) when reading the latest finding in nutrition science ↔ Think twice about new nutrition research findings 预判"对新研究保持怀疑"与 Think twice about new nutrition research findings 在态 度（怀疑↔三思）与对象（最新营养发现↔新营养研究结论）两层都对齐。
